# Benchmark — the machine-checkable rules vs. their canonical examples

<!-- GENERATED by cli/scripts/sync-benchmark.js — do not edit by hand. Regenerate: cd cli && npm run sync:benchmark -->

**Scope, honestly stated:** this is a *self*-benchmark over the repo's curated
[`examples/`](examples/) — one canonical vulnerable/fixed pair per machine-checkable
rule, scanned by the real shipped engine. It proves two properties that CI enforces on
every change (`cli/test/examples.test.js`): the patterns **detect their canonical bug**
(anti-rot) and **stay quiet on the canonical fix** (false-positive discipline, with
documented exclusion-cleared cases where the tripwire is retained by design). It is
**not** a third-party recall benchmark: deterministic patterns catch the bug *classes*
they encode, and deeper semantic review is what the review-only rules and a
[Jelleo audit](https://jelleo.com) are for.

## Scoreboard — 30 machine-checkable rules

- **Detection (anti-rot): 30/30** vulnerable examples fire their rule.
- **FP discipline: 20/30 fixed examples scanner-clean**, 10 exclusion-cleared (tripwire retained by design; the fix satisfies the rule's numbered exclusion).

## How this stays honest

- CI **fails** if a rule stops firing on its vulnerable example (a regex change that
  silently loses detection cannot merge), and **fails** if a fixed example fires
  without a documented exclusion entry (a noisy rule change cannot merge).
- This file is generated; CI fails if it is stale (`sync-benchmark.js --check`).
- The exclusion-cleared list lives in [`examples/fixed-still-fires.json`](examples/fixed-still-fires.json)
  with the specific exclusion each fix satisfies.
